references.text: The preceding verse tells us that the man had been sick for thirty-eight years ([ref:Joh 5:5|John 5:5]). Jesus already knew about the man's long suffering, which shows his supernatural knowledge and compassion.
Jesus knew people and knew what was in them ([ref:Joh 2:24-25|John 2:24-25]). In the same way, he knew here that the man had been sick for a long time without being told.

Jesus' supernatural knowledge of people is also shown in his meeting with Nathanael, where Jesus knew about him before Philip called him ([ref:Joh 1:48|John 1:48]). Here Jesus knows the sick man's situation in the same way.
Later Jesus finds the man in the temple and says that he has been made well ([ref:Joh 5:14|John 5:14]). Jesus' question "Do you want to be made well?" in verse 6 is the introduction to this healing.

Jesus asks a similar question to the blind Bartimaeus: "What do you want me to do for you?" ([ref:Mark 10:51|Mark 10:51]). In both cases, Jesus invites the sick person to express their faith and desire for healing.
Jesus' question about whether the man wanted to be made well was answered in the healing that followed, when Jesus said: "Get up, pick up your mat and walk!" ([ref:Joh 5:8-9|John 5:8-9]).

In his conversation with the Samaritan woman, Jesus reveals that he knows her life story ([ref:Joh 4:17-18|John 4:17-18]). This is another example of Jesus' supernatural knowledge of individual situations, just as he knew the paralyzed man's history.
The Lord presents himself as the one who heals: "I am the Lord your healer" ([ref:2 Mos 15:26|Exodus 15:26]). Jesus' question to the sick man shows him as God's healer who seeks out the suffering.
The psalmist praises the Lord as "who heals all your diseases" ([ref:Sal 103:3|Psalm 103:3]). Jesus fulfills this promise by seeking out and healing the man who had been sick for so many years.
